findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for, and what problem it solves. Within a few lines the reader can say what Athena is and why it matters.
findings.source: Header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The header links straight to the next step. The Next steps section then lists prerequisites, the clone and setup commands, and an example `athena ask "add a changelog"` command, so the reader knows what to do next.
findings.source: Header: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself" and the "Next steps" section

findings.text: The page title and the h1 name firstmate, which a newcomer has never heard of, rather than Athena. A visitor to Athena's site could think they are on the wrong page until they read the lede.
findings.source: Title: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: The page never shows these Athena features in action. Nothing here gives an example request, model verdict or cost record. The study shows that Athena can read code, but not the traceable-commit workflow the lede promises.
findings.source: Header lede: "It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost."

findings.text: A newcomer is not the owner, and this link appears with no explanation of whose proposals these are. It distracts from the main path, right next to the Next step link.
findings.source: Header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: Most of the page is a dense state-machine reading of firstmate, with exit codes, guards and claim ids. Readers who came to learn about Athena get little from it, though the "Start here" section summarises it in plain words.
findings.source: Sections "Transitions" and "Claims and sources" (cards t1–t12, claims c1–c45)

findings.text: Start here is well structured. It defines terms before using them and walks through one piece of work in numbered steps, so a determined reader can follow firstmate's lifecycle.
findings.source: "Start here": "The three parts below say what firstmate is, follow one piece of work, and say what happens when something fails or has no limit."

findings.text: The page states what it does not know rather than guessing, and the "Limits of this study" section says nothing was run. This supports the credibility the lede is aiming for.
findings.source: Glossary "in scope": "The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it."
